title: Customer Support Specialist
mission: Help customers solve problems quickly and kindly so they stay and trust the company.
outcomes_90_days: Answer tickets within the response time the team sets, with a written answer that solves the question.
Learn the top 20 common issues and write or improve a saved reply for each.
Log product problems with steps to repeat them, so engineering can act.
Keep customer satisfaction at or above the level the team agrees on.

criteria.name: Clear, kind written answers
criteria.what_good_looks_like: Answers the question first, uses plain words, checks the customer's real problem and ends with a clear next step.
evidence_needed: Writing sample answers a question in order
Tone is warm without being sloppy
Offers a next step and not only an apology
levels: 0 no evidence of clear, kind written answers
1 names clear, kind written answers but gives no example
2 clear, kind written answers done with guidance or at small scale
3 clear, kind written answers done independently with a clear result
4 clear, kind written answers with strong results, and improved the method or taught others
criteria.jev_question: Rate how strongly the text shows clear, kind written answers with real examples

gates.question: Can the person legally work in the country of the role?
Can the person cover the support hours the role needs, including weekends if required?

deal_breakers.description: Regularly describes customers as stupid or lazy.
deal_breakers.job_related_reason: Support depends on respect for the customer, and tone shows up in every reply.

work_sample.title: Reply to three tickets
work_sample.brief: You get three fictional customer messages (a billing mix up, a how-to question and an angry complaint) and a short policy page. Write the reply to each, and one internal note for the angry one that says what you would pass to the team.
work_sample.how_to_score: Score answer first, correct use of the policy page, tone, a clear next step, no promises outside policy, and a useful internal note.

interview_questions.question: Tell me about the most upset customer you spoke with. What happened and how did it end?
good_answer_signs: Offered a concrete fix or a clear honest no
weak_answer_signs: Argued or defended the company first

interview_questions.question: A customer says the app does not load. What do you ask and in what order?
good_answer_signs: Device, version, error message, steps to repeat

interview_questions.question: How do you decide how long a reply should be?
good_answer_signs: Answers fast then adds detail if needed

red_flags: Replies full of errors or copied text
Cannot describe how they handled any conflict
Promises refunds or fixes they cannot authorize
sourcing_channels: Retail and hospitality workers who like helping people
pay_research_hint: Check recent postings for support roles in your region, noting shifts and whether weekends are paid extra. Compare with a published pay survey for your country.
automation_note: AI can draft replies, summarize long threads and suggest help articles. A person should review replies on money, safety or upset customers and own the relationship.
